AL2023 lists every CUDA 12.x stream (cuda-nvdisasm-12-5/12-6/12-8/12-9) as No Fix Planned for this advisory; only the cuda-13-0 stream is Fixed, and CUDA 12.9 is the image contract for TF 2.21. Exploitation requires running nvdisasm on an attacker-supplied ELF file, which is not part of the training entrypoint. Note that the Dockerfile removes /usr/local/cuda/bin/nvdisasm, but triton 3.6.0 bundles its own nvdisasm under site-packages/triton/backends/nvidia/bin/, so the binary is still present in the GPU image. Revisit when the CUDA base image moves to the 13.x stream.

cuda-toolkit-config-common 12.9.79 ships with the nvidia/cuda:12.9.1-runtime-amzn2023 base image. AL2023 lists every CUDA 12.x stream as No Fix Planned for this advisory; only the cuda-13-0 stream is Fixed, and CUDA 12.9 is the image contract for TF 2.21. Exploitation requires running cuobjdump on an attacker-supplied ELF file, which is not part of the training entrypoint. cuobjdump is retained deliberately for JIT compilation support and is additionally bundled by triton 3.6.0 under site-packages/triton/backends/nvidia/bin/. Revisit when the CUDA base image moves to the 13.x stream.
